subject: QBR prep: capacity prioritization + token economics snapshot
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ethan Morris <ethan@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: capacity prioritization + token economics snapshot

Team — putting together the leadership QBR slide set this week. Primary asks below; I’d like concise bullets and one slide/table per owner by EOD Friday so I can synthesize. High-level goal: give execs a clear call on what capacity actions we need to pursue for H2 and the expected impact on unit economics.

Quick context: Acme Health expansion is gating our Dedicated commit conversation — they want predictable latency and a clear cost model. We also need to show runway for our hosted API during the expected holiday traffic spike.

Asks (prioritized):
- Vivek: one slide with 3 capacity scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive) showing committed GPUs, expected avg utilization, and tail-latency risk. Include estimated monthly GPU spend per scenario.
- Rishi: one slide summarizing unit-econ levers — batching, KV prefix cache coverage, quantization ops — and estimated $/1000 tokens under each lever. Short sensitivity table please.
- Olga: ops readiness checklist for burst windows (autoscale thresholds, warm pools, cross-region fallback) and a 2-line risk statement per item.

Attachments: initial draft deck and a raw snapshot (gpu_econ_snapshot_aug15.csv) with per-cluster utilization and cost lines. I pasted a short table in the slide notes for reference.

Timing: goal to lock the internal QBR narrative Mon 8/20 so I can route to CEO/Finance on 8/21.

Thanks — Lauren

[Attachment: 20280815-qbr-deck-draft.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: gpu_econ_snapshot_aug15.csv (csv)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ethan Morris <ethan@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity prioritization + token economics snapshot

Thanks Lauren — attaching the capacity snapshot and scenario table. High-level notes first:

- Baseline (recommended): commit 120 A100-equivalent GPUs across two regions. Expected steady-state avg utilization ~62%. Estimated monthly GPU spend: $1.1M. Tail latency (99.9th) manageable with autoscale to burst pool but needs warm nodes.
- Conservative: keep current 90 GPUs, rely on aggressive autoscaling to burst. Avg utilization ~72% (higher), but tail-latency risk increases (~double) during sustained spikes; monthly spend ~0.85M but higher customer SLAs risk.
- Aggressive: reserve 160 GPUs to cover peak + buffer; utilization drops to ~48%, spend ~1.45M, but we can guarantee tighter latency SLOs and simpler routing.

Tradeoffs: committing more capacity reduces tail-latency but raises cost and reduces overall % utilization. Batching improvements can recover ~8-12% effective throughput (see column in CSV), prefix KV caching saves ~10-15% token computation cost for chat-heavy workloads.

I included an "ops ask" column listing warm pool sizes and recommended autoscale windows. Spreadsheet attached.

[Attachment: gpu_econ_snapshot_aug15.csv (csv)]

Vivek

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity prioritization + token economics snapshot

Lauren / team — quick ops readiness checklist (short form) below. I kept it tight since the deck will only show one risk line per item.

- Warm pool sizing: for baseline scenario, recommend warm pool = 12% of committed capacity (pre-warmed instances across regions). Risk: underestimating cold-starts during multi-region failovers.
- Autoscale thresholds: set scale-up at 70% CPU-GPU queue fill sustained for 90s; scale-down after 5m idle. Risk: oscillation if thresholds too tight.
- Cross-region failover: test runbook weekly during spike window; risk: transient DNS propagation adding ~150-300ms.
- Cache priming (KV): schedule a daily priming job for top-500 prefixes pre-peak to avoid cold-prefix penalties. Risk: priming costs and stale entries.

I can convert each bullet into a 1-line risk for the slide. Also attached a short latency/batching tradeoffs workbook — it has a small sim that demonstrates how 2x batching reduces cost-per-token by ~9% but lifts P99 by ~120ms on our current kernel mix.

[Attachment: batching_latency-tradeoffs.xlsx (xlsx)]

— Olga

Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity prioritization + token economics snapshot

Appended my unit-econ summary (short). I focused on the three levers you asked for and included conservative / expected / optimistic estimates for each. See numbers below and attached quick-model.

Summary (per 1,000 tokens):
- Baseline (no levers): $0.95 / 1k tokens (hosted mix: 70% chat, 30% single-turn generate).
- With batching (mid rollout): $0.85 / 1k tokens (assumes average batching gain 10%, P50 latency ~unchanged, P99 +80ms).
- With KV prefix cache (50% coverage): $0.78 / 1k tokens (saves ~12% compute ops on chat-heavy items).
- Quantization (mixed ops): $0.72 / 1k tokens (assumes 4-bit quantization for lower-compute variants on 30% of requests).

Sensitivity notes: combining batching + KV can push to ~$0.66 / 1k tokens in optimistic case, but note operational tradeoffs: more batching increases P99 and customer-facing latency unless we expand warm pools. I attached a 3-tab workbook with assumptions and the sensitivity grid.

I propose we present the baseline vs "combined lever" columns in the QBR slide and call out the operational asks (warm pool + priming + small quant rollout). If you want, I can mock a single slide with the table.

[Attachment: batching_latency-tradeoffs.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: gpu_econ_snapshot_aug15.csv (csv)]
